method: Independent headless Chromium, actual locally served application without response overrides. Each pose awaited no tile loading, no staging/pending geometry, no native bank transaction and no dirty source surfaces, then four consecutive identical graphics/frontier/source/surface/frame snapshots. A subsequent 2200ms paused interval preceded the raw PNG.

findings.detail: All seven district source targets are detailed on desktop and mobile after settling, including MET 6939524390 and 6939524400. No visible foreground building holes or doubled buildings were found in these twenty static images.
Building bases have restrained contact darkening. Contacts are a single source-contour lighting batch and do not replace source geometry. Courtyard 27724113 has quiet paving on desktop and mobile.
Visible Miass water is continuous at its bank and has small ripples without the earlier coherent stripes or flat source-fragment patch. This framing does not include the entire bridge.
MET detailed metal roofs still contain recognizable, repeated diagonal diffuse marks. Their repetition remains visible on both viewport sizes.

Broad untextured gray-beige land between KAL, SOV and LEN buildings, and hard polygon transitions elsewhere, leave large portions of the city looking like a diagram. Contact shading improves anchoring but does not supply convincing ground surfaces.
Facade color, window rhythm and roof-equipment spacing remain overly uniform across otherwise distinct architecture. The close courtyard roof occupies much of the view as a large repetitive plane.

CEN and MET source vegetation has recognizably regular spacing and very similar crown silhouettes. Coordinate placement uses a fixed 30 Mercator-metre grid with jitter confined to the middle half of each cell.

On mobile, the existing header, movement status, time controls and statistics drawer leave limited visible map area. Screenshots preserve the actual UI; no UI redesign is included in this art assessment.
CEN foreground tree crown appears near the road edge. No source-coordinate overlap of trunk or clearance zone is asserted from the screenshot.

recommendedNextBoundedChanges: Verify the exact source classes under the large flat ground regions before extending metric materials. Preserve those actual polygon boundaries, holes and water/road ordering; do not invent vegetation or paved land classifications.

Reduce remaining recognizable corrugated_iron diffuse stamp contrast while preserving pinned CC0 asset URLs, physical UV scale and physically filtered normal/roughness. Recheck MET desktop/mobile before accepting.

Replace the middle-half grid jitter for area-derived trees with a deterministic source-contained placement scheme that avoids regular rows while retaining exact source tree points, road/building clearance and caps.
limitations: junctionTraffic.ts changed during capture. All other captured runtime sources and the catalogue remained unchanged; traffic motion is a separate gate.
SwiftShader and background development activity; no FPS, physical mobile-device performance or hardware renderer claim.
Twenty settled static screenshots do not prove continuous zoom, cache eviction, WebGL recovery, picking or traffic safety.
Seven district samples are actual source-building poses, not exhaustive visual validation of every city block.
The complete bridge is outside the waterfront framing. No bridge traversal acceptance is claimed.
Raw PNGs and telemetry remain local QA artifacts; portable filenames and SHA-256 hashes are recorded without absolute local paths.
